tldr_text:
Localized curfews begin Monday evening in several French cities, including Lille, Douai, and Wattigni, following widespread rioting and looting over the weekend. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced the partial measures, stating they were better adapted than a nationwide state of emergency, which he did not rule out if violence continued. President Emmanuel Macron refused Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's offer to resign, instructing him to address security failures.

Protesters blocked the entrance to the Louvre in Paris on Monday, fueled by grievances over the cost of living, inflation, education conditions, and declining public services.

Iran-backed Houthi rebels struck Yemeni government forces with ballistic missiles on Monday, killing at least 53 soldiers at the al-Alam military camp in Shabwa province. The attack wounded an additional 200 recruits. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree confirmed the group targeted the camp, claiming it was run by Saudi forces. The provincial government in Shabwa stated the death toll is preliminary and may rise.

Trump stated that if Israel chooses a leader other than Netanyahu, the United States would have to confront Iran alone, a task he is not inclined to undertake. Netanyahu thanked Trump for his support, pledging to "complete the mission" together.

Independent MP Helen Haines remains in critical condition after being struck by a car outside her Wangaratta office on Monday afternoon. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described the incident as an "apparent attack" and a "deliberate act," not an accident. Victoria Police activated the Joint Counter Terrorism Team, which includes the Australian Federal Police, Victoria Police, and ASIO, to investigate the incident. A 43-year-old man was arrested at the scene, and a knife was seized from inside the vehicle.

A Kenyan court convicted self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie and 28 associates of murdering 191 people, including 190 children, in the Shakahola starvation cult case. The court rejected the defense's argument that the victims voluntarily fasted to death. Hundreds of bodies, totaling over 400, have been recovered from the Shakahola Forest since 2023. Post-mortems indicated many victims died from starvation, but also from asphyxia, neck compression, and traumatic head injuries.

The US Supreme Court on Monday rejected an appeal by Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the accused mastermind of the September 11, 2001, attacks, and two co-defendants to revive a 2024 plea deal. The agreement would have spared Mohammed, Mustafa al Hawsawi, and Walid bin 'Atash the death penalty in exchange for guilty pleas. Former Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin revoked the plea deals in 2024, two days after they were offered and accepted.

The Supreme Court agreed on Monday to review a Reconstruction-era ban on distilling spirits in private homes. The court will consider whether Congress had the constitutional authority to impose the 1868 ban. Federal law makes home distilling a crime punishable by up to five years in prison and a $10,000 fine, with violators' homes and property also subject to forfeiture. The government collected $11.1 billion in alcohol taxes in fiscal year 2023, with $6.8 billion from distilled spirits.

Former President Barack Obama on Sunday called the federal criminal investigation into Representative Ilhan Omar "appalling," stating the Trump administration is bringing the full weight of the federal government against an elected official for criticizing the president. Federal agents raided Omar's Washington, D.C., home as part of the investigation into her immigration status. White House border czar Tom Homan stated investigators have a "strong case" against Omar, confirming denaturalization and deportation are potential consequences for immigration fraud.

## OPEN
A: From Void News, this is On Air. It's Monday, October nineteenth. French authorities have ordered curfews in several cities as widespread unrest continues.

## MENU
A: On the desk today.
A: France orders localized curfews amid widespread riots.
B: An Australian M-P is critically injured in an apparent car attack.
A: Israel arrests ten settlers after West Bank attacks.
B: The Supreme Court rejects a nine-eleven mastermind's plea deal.
A: A Kenyan cult leader has been convicted of murdering one hundred ninety-one followers.

## STORY 1 | France Curfews and Riots
A: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has announced localized and partial curfews in several cities. These measures address widespread rioting and looting over the weekend. The Prime Minister says these curfews are better adapted than a nationwide state of emergency. He did not rule out a national state of emergency if violence continues.
A: Curfews begin this evening in some areas. This includes Lille and the surrounding towns of Douai, Wattignies, and Denain. These curfews run from eight in the evening to six in the morning. Authorities in Marseille already banned gatherings and demonstrations from noon to eight this evening.
A: The unrest has led to approximately two thousand four hundred arrests. Some reports indicate more than two thousand five hundred arrests. President Emmanuel Macron refused Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's offer to resign. He instructed the minister to address security failures.
A: The Prime Minister attributes the unrest to the extreme-left and criminal elements. He says there is an agenda of chaos to disrupt next year’s presidential election. He announced a strong judicial response to crack down on violence and crime. Investigators are reviewing social media footage.
B: Middle East Eye reports two people dead and two protesters losing hands to stun grenades.

## STORY 2 | Australian M-P Attacked
B: In Australia, Independent M-P Helen Haines remains in critical condition. She was struck by a car outside her Wangaratta office this afternoon. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described the incident as an apparent attack. He called it a deliberate act, stating it was not an accident.
B: Victoria Police are investigating whether the act was intentional. They have activated the Joint Counter Terrorism Team. This team includes the Australian Federal Police, Victoria Police, and A-S-I-O. Ms. Haines, who is sixty-five, was airlifted to a Melbourne hospital with critical injuries.
B: The incident occurred around three thirty-five this afternoon on Murphy Street. Witnesses reported hearing a bang. They saw a woman pinned between two cars. One bystander detained the driver. A forty-three-year-old man was arrested at the scene. Police seized a knife from inside the vehicle.
A: Some sources highlight the activation of the counter-terror team in their headlines.

## STORY 3 | Israel Settler Arrests
A: Israeli security forces have arrested ten suspected extremist settlers in the occupied West Bank. The arrests followed attacks on a U-S journalist and European diplomats. These attacks sparked international condemnation. The suspects were detained during a joint operation called Olive Leaf. This operation involved police, the Shin Bet security agency, and the I-D-F.
A: Israeli Police Commissioner Danny Levy says the law in Judea and Samaria applies to everyone. He says this is regardless of identity or affiliation. Major General Moshe Finchi, the Israeli police's West Bank commander, says suspects were arrested on suspicion of involvement in violent incidents. They are also suspected of violating a military commander’s order.
A: Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was beaten on Friday. She sustained multiple injuries including broken vertebrae and a rib. A convoy of European diplomats was also attacked over the weekend. Al Jazeera's investigation challenges official Israeli narratives regarding the attack on Heidi Levine. It states that verified footage and mapped coordinates reveal a coordinated attack by masked settlers. Israeli military vehicles reportedly passed by without intervening.
B: U-S Secretary of State Marco Rubio called for Israel to crack down on violence.

## STORY 4 | Supreme Court Rejects Plea
B: The U-S Supreme Court has declined to hear a bid by Khalid Sheikh Mohammed. He sought to revive a two thousand twenty-four plea agreement. This agreement would have spared him the death penalty in exchange for a guilty plea.
B: The justices turned away appeals by Mohammed and two co-defendants. These co-defendants are Mustafa al Hawsawi and Walid bin 'Atash. They had also signed plea agreements. The Supreme Court's unsigned opinion did not explain why the appeal was rejected. Justice Brett Kavanaugh recused himself from the decision.
B: Former Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin scrapped the plea deals. He did this two days after they were offered and accepted. A U-S official overseeing military commissions had accepted the deals. The Supreme Court's denial keeps the death penalty on the table for the accused nine-eleven plotters.
A: Justice Brett Kavanaugh did not participate in the court's consideration of the appeal.

## BRIEFS
A: Also on the desk.
A: Paul Mackenzie and twenty-eight associates have been found guilty of murdering one hundred ninety-one people, including one hundred ninety children, in Kenya.
A: Protesters blocked the entrance to the Louvre in Paris today as France grapples with widespread social unrest.
B: Fifty investigators are probing a fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta that killed four service members.
B: The Supreme Court agreed today to review a federal ban on distilling spirits in private homes, a Reconstruction-era law.
A: Houthi rebels launched a ballistic missile attack on a military training camp in Yemen's Shabwa province, killing at least fifty-three soldiers.
A: President Donald Trump signed an executive order today establishing a new Women's Health Division at the N-I-H and a White House task force.
B: Former President Barack Obama publicly criticized a federal criminal investigation into Representative Ilhan Omar, calling it appalling.

## FINALLY | 10 | Women's Health Initiative
B: One more before Void Opinion. President Donald Trump signed an executive order today establishing a new Women's Health Division at the National Institutes of Health. The order also creates a White House Women's Health Task Force. First Lady Melania Trump reportedly pushed for this action. She joined the President for the signing ceremony in the Rose Garden. The division will aim to increase scientific review of women's health conditions, advance and coordinate research, and promote innovation.

opinion_text:
France has imposed localized curfews across several cities, including Lille, Douai, Wattignies, and Denain, from 8:00 pm to 6:00 am. Marseille authorities already banned gatherings and demonstrations from noon to 8 pm. These measures follow widespread rioting and looting that led to approximately 2,400 arrests. Nearly 1,000 emergency personnel sustained injuries. At least 3,000 businesses suffered damage.

The unrest itself followed weeks of protests concerning rising living costs, deteriorating public services, and school conditions. These are areas where state provision and regulation are central. The state's chosen path of escalating control, while addressing immediate symptoms of disorder, imposes costs on individual liberty and economic freedom. We see this as a dangerous precedent.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu stated these partial curfews were "better adapted" than a nationwide state of emergency, yet he did not rule out broader measures if violence persisted. This incremental expansion of authority directly restricts the movement and economic activity of citizens. The damage to thousands of businesses represents a direct assault on private enterprise and the livelihoods of individuals, a cost borne by the productive sector. President Emmanuel Macron refused Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's offer to resign, instructing him to address security failures. This decision maintains the existing leadership structure despite acknowledged shortcomings in maintaining public order.

Maintaining public order is a foundational responsibility of any government. However, the methods employed and the underlying causes of the unrest demand scrutiny. The solution of curfews and mass arrests, while quelling immediate violence, does not address the systemic issues that fueled the protests. Instead, it places the burden of state failure onto the individual citizen and private business, restricting their freedoms and economic opportunities. We must question whether the architects of these policies will ever face the second-order effects of their decisions.

The ripple effects extend beyond France's borders. Italy, for instance, has already approved an emergency anti-riot order. This suggests that the French response, rather than being an isolated incident, sets a precedent for other nations to adopt similar expansions of state power in the face of internal dissent. We must ask what long-term costs these measures impose on the fabric of free societies, and whether the cure of concentrated authority ultimately proves more debilitating than the disease it purports to treat.
